newsitem.title: UK: Kingfisher dips on profit-taking after data.
newsitem.headline: Kingfisher dips on profit-taking after data.

text.p: Shares in Kingfisher Plc were down 5p at 665p by 0855 GMT as investors took profits after a recent good run, dealers and analysts said.
On Wednesday the retailer said like-for-like sales rose 7.8 percent in the nine weeks to January 4, 1997, toward the top of analysts expectations.
"Kingfisher had pretty good support ahead of the figures. We're just seeing some profit-taking," the head of trading at a major investment bank said.
Nick Bubb, stores analyst at Mees Pierson expects Kingfisher shares to push towards 750p in the medium term.
"The shares may consolidate for awhile, but the sales figures were quite favourable. It was generally a good performance," Bubb said.
Bubb has increased his full-year pre-tax profits forecast on Kingfisher to 380 million stg from 375 million stg.
